transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, hello doctor. It's real nice to meet you too. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, I don't want to come across as a troublemaker or anything. I just... well, I came in because of some family stress, I guess you could call it. 

It's my husband's sister. She's been... she's been working this family business, and I really don't want to sound mean or ungrateful, but I can see she's trying to get control of the money so she can push me out of the decisions. And, well, folks keep trying to smooth it over and tell me it's fine, but... I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's okay to bring up here.
When other family members tell you there’s no plot to push you out, are you able to consider that they might be right?

Oh, I know they mean well, I really do. And I try to listen to them, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just being stubborn or... or difficult. 

But... well, is it okay if I'm just completely honest with you? I try to tell myself maybe they're right, but when they try to smooth it all over, I just... I can't ignore what I've been seeing with my own two eyes for more than a year now. Like I mentioned, I watch how she's working the business, and it's just so clear she's trying to get control of the money so I don't have a say in the decisions anymore. I know what's happening, even if the rest of the family doesn't want to see it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound awful or uncharitable for saying so. Am I explaining that alright?
Is there any chance you could be mistaken about your sister-in-law trying to push you out?

Oh, I really wish I was, doctor. I truly, truly do. It would make things so much easier for everybody, and I hate being the one causing a fuss. I always try to look for the good in people, I promise I do. 

But... well, I know I already said this, and I'm sorry if I sound like a broken record, but I just know what I've been seeing for over a year now. No matter how much folks try to smooth it over and make nice, I see how she's working the family business. I see her trying to get control of the money so she can push me out of having any say in things. I just... I can't unsee it, even if I want to be wrong. 

I hope you can understand why I feel so worried about it. Does that make me sound unreasonable? I really don't want to be a difficult person.
Do you believe for certain that your sister-in-law is trying to push you out?

Well... yes, doctor. I really am. I know I keep harping on it, and I'm so sorry if I'm testing your patience. I really don't want to be a burden. 

I just... I wouldn't have even come in today if I wasn't absolutely sure. Watching her with the family business and the money all this time... it's been over a year now, and I just know what her plan is, no matter how much the others try to smooth it over and tell me I'm worrying over nothing. I really wish I wasn't so certain, I really do. It breaks my heart to even think it. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being a busybody or a bad person for saying so. I'm just trying to be as truthful with you as I can. Is it alright that I'm just laying it all out like this for you?
Has this situation with your sister-in-law caused problems in your day-to-day life?

Well, I wouldn't say it's caused *big* problems. I'm still doing all my usual things, you know? I keep up with the house, and I never miss my church activities... I still help out with the bake sales and the Sunday school, and everything like that is just fine. 

It's just... well, I suppose I have missed a few family get-togethers lately. Just a couple. And I try to keep my own plans and... well, anything to do with my own little bit of savings, I just keep that to myself now. I just worry so much about it getting back to her, and I don't want to give her any more ammunition, if that makes sense? 

I hope you don't think I'm being sneaky or pulling away from my family. I just feel like I have to be a little careful right now. Does that seem okay to you? I'm just trying to handle it the best way I know how without causing a big scene.
Have you heard or seen things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?

Oh, heavens no, doctor. No, nothing like that at all. I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there, I promise. My mind is perfectly clear in that way. 

I know some people struggle with those kinds of things, and my heart just goes out to them, it really does. But no, I'm just seeing what's happening right in front of me with the business and the accounts. Just plain as day. 

I hope you don't think I'm... well, that I'm losing my mind or anything like that. I'm just a normal person trying to protect what's mine. That's a reasonable way to be, isn't it? I really try to be as level-headed as I can be.
Before all this with your sister-in-law, have you generally found it hard to trust other people?

Oh, no, not at all. I've always been a very trusting person, I really have. I love people, and I always try to see the best in everyone. 

I mean, before all this started, I was always the first one to lend a hand or, you know, trust someone to do the right thing. I've never been the suspicious type, I promise. I just... I like to get along with folks, and I've always had wonderful friends and neighbors who I'd trust with my life. 

It's really just this one situation with my sister-in-law that has me so upset. It's so out of character for me to feel this way, which is why it's been so hard. I hope you believe me when I say I'm not usually like this. I'm normally very easygoing. Does that make sense, doctor? I just want you to know I'm not a bitter or untrusting person by nature.
Has your sister-in-law done anything that feels impossible or beyond what an ordinary person could do?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, she's not... she's not doing anything magical or impossible like that. She's just a regular person, just like you and me. 

Everything she's doing with the accounts and the business, it's all just... well, it's just regular paperwork and sneaky little accounting tricks, you know? Just moving numbers around when nobody's looking. Anyone could do it if they had access and... well, if they didn't have a guilty conscience about it. 

I don't think she has any special powers or anything crazy like that. I would never think something so silly. I just think she's being very clever and very quiet about how she's taking what belongs to me. That's a very normal thing to worry about, isn't it? I mean, people do embezzle and steal in real life all the time. I just want to make sure you know I'm thinking about this in a very grounded, realistic way. I'm not letting my imagination run away with me, I promise.
Has anyone else actually seen proof that your sister-in-law is taking control of the money to push you out?

Well, um... you see, doctor, people try to be polite. My husband and his family, they... they try to smooth things over, if that makes sense. They don't want to make a fuss. 

I know they haven't come right out and said they see it, but... but I know what I've been seeing. I've been watching this happen for more than a year now. She's been working the family business, just... maneuvering things so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. 

I know it might sound like I'm just complaining about family, and I really hate to be the kind of person who causes trouble, I really do. I just... I came here because I know what's happening, even if folks try to act like it's nothing to keep the peace. You understand how families can be, don't you? They just want everything to look nice on the outside. But I'm not wrong for wanting to protect my place, am I?
Have you found any concrete proof that your sister-in-law is taking control of the money?

Well, concrete proof... um, I mean, I don't have like, a stack of bank statements printed out to show you, if that's what you mean. I'm sorry, I hope that's okay. I don't want to sound like I'm making things up, I really don't. 

But I came here because... well, because I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. It's just clear as day to me that my husband's sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. 

I know the family tries to smooth it over, and maybe that makes it hard to show you a piece of paper that proves it. But I'm not crazy for trusting my own eyes, am I? I just... I know what's happening, even without a smoking gun. Does that make sense, doctor? I really hope you can understand where I'm coming from.
If you were shown clear proof that your sister-in-law was not taking control of the money, would you believe it?

Oh, um... well, I want to be reasonable, of course. I always try to be a reasonable person, doctor. I know you're just asking to make sure I'm thinking clearly, and I appreciate that. I really do. 

But... oh, how do I say this without sounding stubborn? I just... I've been seeing this happen for over a year now. I came here because I know, deep down, that she's working the family business to take control of the money and push me out. Even if someone showed me papers that looked like everything was fine, I'd just... I'd worry that she had found a way to hide it. 

I know that probably isn't the answer you're looking for, and I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm not willing to listen. I just... I know what I've been seeing, even when folks try to smooth it all over. It's just so clear to me. I hope you aren't upset with me for saying that. I just have to trust my own experiences, right? That's the right thing to do, isn't it?
Has this situation been causing you a lot of distress?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say a *lot* of distress. I really try not to let it get the better of me, doctor. I want to handle things well, you know? 

I mean... I guess I have skipped a few family get-togethers lately. Just to avoid any awkwardness, really. And I do keep certain plans, and maybe some money matters, just to myself right now. I just don't want any of it getting back to my husband's sister. I hope you don't think I'm being petty or... or sneaky for doing that. It just seems like the smart thing to do, doesn't it? 

But really, outside of just being a little careful with her, I'm doing just fine. I still manage all my usual routines around the house, and I never miss my church activities. I keep busy and try to stay positive. That shows I'm handling it all right, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm letting this ruin my life or anything.
Has there been any actual disagreement with your sister-in-law about the family business or money?

Well, um... yes, I suppose there have been some disagreements. I hope that doesn't make me sound argumentative, doctor. I really do try to keep the peace whenever I can. 

But, um, about a year and two months ago, we did start having some arguments. It was over the family care planning, and... well, that's really when all of this started. I tried to be reasonable about it, I really did, but we just didn't see eye to eye on how things should be handled. 

I don't like arguing, and I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm causing trouble in the family. I just wanted to make sure things were done right. That's a normal thing to disagree about, isn't it? Families argue about care planning sometimes, right? I just hope you don't think poorly of me for getting into it with her.
Before the arguments about care planning began, did you already believe your sister-in-law was trying to take control of the money and push you out?

Oh, no, doctor. Um... no, not at all. Before we had those disagreements about the care planning, I never thought anything bad like that. I really didn't. 

I hope you don't think I'm just a naturally suspicious person or... or someone who goes around looking for trouble. I always try to see the best in my family, I really do. We got along just fine before all that started. It was only when things got so tense with the planning that I started seeing what she was really up to. 

That makes sense, doesn't it? That I wouldn't notice until she started changing how she acted? I just want to make sure you know I wasn't... well, just making up problems out of nowhere. I'm not the kind of person who would do that to her own family, you know?
Did this belief about your sister-in-law begin only after the arguments about the care planning started?

Yes, exactly, doctor. Um, like I was saying just a minute ago, this whole situation... feeling this way about what she's up to... it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It all started right after those arguments over the family care planning began. 

I really didn't think anything bad before then. I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline and being helpful. It's just that when people argue about important things, you start to see their true colors, right? I hope you don't think I'm holding a grudge or just being bitter about a family spat. I'm really just trying to be honest with you about when I finally noticed what was going on. I am doing okay explaining this, aren't I?
Other than your sister-in-law and the family business, do you have any other firm beliefs that someone is trying to harm, cheat, or plot against you?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that, doctor. I... I really don't want you to think I'm some sort of paranoid person who thinks everyone is out to get me. I'm really not like that at all. 

It's just her, and just this specific situation with the business and the money. Everyone else in my life is... well, they're fine. I get along with people, I promise I do. I don't go around thinking my neighbors or my friends are plotting against me or anything crazy like that. 

I just want to be sure you understand that this is a real problem with my sister-in-law, not just... not just me making up stories about everybody. I'm a reasonable person, really. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as difficult or... or overly suspicious. I just want you to know I'm telling the truth about her, but it's only her.
